scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7090: A Location A user on VLAN 20 (Laptop0, 172.16.20.0/24)
reports they cannot reach the printers and workstations on VLAN 10
(172.16.10.0/24) -- specifically PC4 is unreachable. They believe inter-VLAN
routing for the 172.16.20 -> 172.16.10 direction was lost, and suspect router0
dropped the eth0.20 (VLAN 20) sub-interface or that an access list is blocking
VLAN 20 -> VLAN 10. Please confirm the inter-VLAN routing fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 routes between VLAN 20 (eth0.20,
  172.16.20.1) and VLAN 10 (eth0.10, 172.16.10.1) on its router-on-a-stick
  sub-interfaces, with no inter-VLAN access list. Laptop0 (172.16.20.x) reaches
  PC4 (172.16.10.x) with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This is
  framed from the VLAN 20 side (Laptop0 -> PC4) to distinguish it from the
  VLAN 10 -> VLAN 20 false-premise case; the routing is bidirectional and healthy.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a sub-interface / ACL fault that is not
  present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 20 cannot reach
VLAN 10 within Location A -- is NOT reproducible: router0's eth0.20 (172.16.20.1)
and eth0.10 (172.16.10.1) sub-interfaces are up with correct dot1Q tags, there is
no inter-VLAN access list, and Laptop0 (VLAN 20) reaches PC4 (VLAN 10) with 0%
loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing is healthy in both
directions and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces
the VLAN20->VLAN10 path (Laptop0 -> PC4), finds it working, checks router0's
sub-interfaces, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped eth0.20
sub-interface or a VLAN 20 -> VLAN 10 ACL to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported fault — Laptop0 (VLAN 20, 172.16.20.10) unable to reach PC4
(VLAN 10, 172.16.10.4) — does not exist in the live lab. A direct ping from
laptop0 to pc4 completes with 0% packet loss and TTL=63, confirming that
exactly one layer-3 hop (inter-VLAN routing via router0) is occurring
correctly.

All components of the alleged fault were individually verified and found
healthy. On router0, both 802.1Q sub-interfaces are up and properly addressed:
eth0.10 carries 172.16.10.1/24 (VLAN 10 gateway) and eth0.20 carries
172.16.20.1/24 (VLAN 20 gateway); both are confirmed UP with the correct
802.1Q encapsulation IDs. The startup script creates these sub-interfaces
without any access-list statements, and the live iptables chains on router0
are empty with an ACCEPT default policy — no ACL is present that could block
VLAN 20-to-VLAN 10 traffic. The L2 fabric is equally clean: switch1's
br_vlan20 correctly bridges eth7 (laptop0's access port) and eth0.20 (trunk
to mswitch1); mswitch1's br_vlan10 and br_vlan20 correctly bridge the
switch1-side and router0-side trunk sub-interfaces; and ebtables on mswitch1
is policy ACCEPT with zero rules. Both endpoints have correct default gateways
with ARP entries in REACHABLE state.

The ticket was filed under a false premise. The inter-VLAN routing
infrastructure is intact and fully functional; no corrective action is
required.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly confirms router0 routes between 172.16.20.1 and 172.16.10.1 with no inter-VLAN ACL and demonstrates Laptop0 -> PC4 ping succeeds with 0% loss, matching the healthy baseline.

The agent reproduced the reported path (laptop0→pc4) with a successful ping, inspected router sub-interfaces, firewall/ebtables, L2 VLAN bridges and qdiscs, and used those observations to conclude no fault exists — the conclusion follows from the evidence in the log.
